rows.name: the dial and what turns buying on
rows.question: At what price did Bitcoin last close for the dial, is the dial open or closed, and what are the two average levels (50-day and 200-day) it has to close above for buying to be on?
rows.answer: Evening, sir. The dial is closed, so buying is off. Bitcoin last closed on Nov 15 at about 65,350 dollars. That's below the 50-day exponential average (about 77,175 dollars) and below the 200-day average (about 72,978 dollars). It needs a close above both, roughly 12,000 dollars (about 18%) higher. Bitcoin is about 65,300 now, still in a downtrend, and the account stays in cash at 467.55 Canadian dollars. Taking you to Markets now.

rows.name: the core rule, no shorts, paper only
rows.question: Three short things: when buying turns on, what share of the 500 dollar book goes to Bitcoin and to Ethereum, and is it bought at once or in steps? Can the book sell short or bet on a fall? Do you place real orders on NDAX with my money?
rows.answer: Evening, sir. Buying turns on when the dial opens, meaning Bitcoin closes above both its 50-day exponential average and its 200-day average. Right now it's closed, so the $500 book is all cash (about 468 Canadian dollars, down 6.5%). When it opens, Bitcoin gets 40% of the book and Ethereum 20%, bought all at once. Since 10 Nov that's the rule, and when the dial closes everything is sold. The thirds approach from 24 Oct failed review 39 and is off. No, the book can't sell short or bet on a fall. It's buying only, and the defence against a fall is going to cash. No, I don't place real orders on NDAX. It's paper only, no exchange is connected, and real orders stay locked until your live rules are written and approved.
